**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-8932504, Reactome:R-HSA-5083628, Reactome:R-HSA-8932506, Reactome:R-HSA-9939291)

**Proposed mechanism:** POMGNT1 (HGNC:9217) —DISRUPTS→ dystroglycan glycosylation (GO:0035124); dystroglycan glycosylation (GO:0035124) —LEADS_TO→ Congenital muscular dystrophy (HP:0003198); DAG1 (HGNC:2387) —DISRUPTS→ dystroglycan glycosylation (GO:0035124); dystroglycan glycosylation (GO:0035124) —LEADS_TO→ Brain malformations (HP:0000700); dystroglycan glycosylation (GO:0035124) —LEADS_TO→ Eye anomalies (HP:0000479). Loss-of-function mutations in either POMGNT1 or DAG1 disrupt the glycosylation of dystroglycan, a key component of the dystrophin-glycoprotein complex. This disruption leads to a shared downstream phenotype affecting muscle, brain, and eye development.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of pathogenic loss-of-function variants in POMGNT1 or DAG1 in patients with disease A, and pathogenic loss-of-function variants in POMGNT1 or DAG1 in patients with disease B, would support this hypothesis. Conversely, if disease A is found to be caused by a gain-of-function mutation in POMGNT1, or disease B by a gain-of-function mutation in DAG1, this hypothesis would be falsified.

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of dystroglycan glycosylation in both diseases could lead to therapeutic strategies targeting this pathway for both conditions.
